_meta.description: Neighbouring livestock holdings a downgraded food-grade pulse lot can be placed with, as a direct local replacement for imported South American soybean meal. This is the counterparty side of the fallback contract that turns the farmer's worst case from a loss into a floor.
_meta.what_is_real: Locations are actual IGN ADMINEXPRESS commune centroids, so every distance reported by the matcher is a real distance between real places. The NUMBER of holdings per department is scaled by the share of that department's cadastral area that is not in the Agreste COP sheet, which is a measured proxy for its grass and forage area.
_meta.what_is_not_real: Individual holdings are generated. Names are constructed, and herd type and herd size are drawn from published French per-herd-type averages with a fixed seed. No real farm is described. A cooperative deploying this would substitute its own livestock member list; the matching logic is unchanged by that substitution.

dairy_cattle.note: Ruminant. Tolerates raw pulses well; the binding limit is ration protein balance, not anti-nutritional factors.

beef_cattle.note: Ruminant, lowest concentrate demand per head, so a large herd is needed to absorb a lot.

sheep.note: Ruminant. Small absolute demand; useful for small downgraded lots.

pigs.note: Monogastric, high concentrate demand but capped share: raw pulses carry anti-nutritional factors and need inclusion limits.

poultry.note: Monogastric, highest concentrate demand per UGB and the tightest inclusion limit. Also the biggest non-GMO soy buyer, so the substitution is most valuable here.

_meta.concentrate_definition: annual_protein_meal_demand_t is PURCHASED protein concentrate, which is what a pulse displaces. It is not total ration: most of a ruminant ration is home-grown forage and is not addressable.
_meta.max_pulse_intake_note: Capped by herd type. Raw pulses carry anti-nutritional factors - trypsin inhibitors, tannins, vicine in fava bean - so monogastric inclusion is limited to 15-22 percent of concentrate and ruminants to about 30-35 percent. A lot larger than the cap cannot all be placed with one holding, and the matcher says so instead of pretending otherwise.

matching.max_haul_km_note: Beyond roughly 25 km of road distance the haulage on a low-value feed lot eats the premium the breeder is paying over the commodity feed price, and the trade stops making sense for either party.
matching.farmer_share_note: The pulse is worth more to the breeder than the feed spot price, because it replaces purchased soybean meal AND purchased cereal and avoids haulage and trader margin on both. That surplus has to be split. 0.55 to the farmer is a negotiating assumption, stated so it can be argued with: the engine reports both parties' side of the trade so neither is hidden.
matching.min_viable_uplift_note: Below roughly 5 EUR/t the premium does not cover the cost of having a contract at all: sampling and analysis to agree a protein and moisture basis, the haulage arrangement, and the administration on both sides. A 3 EUR/t 'contract' is noise presented as de-risking, so the engine reports no contract rather than quoting one. Stated as a parameter instead of a threshold buried in code because it is a judgement about transaction costs, not a measurement.
